text:
sarah (support): Customer on private deployment reports sudden 401s from the API after a key rotation. They pasted their header from the failing request: 

Customer (from ticket):
`Authorization: ApiKey sk_live_abc123XYZ;`

sarah (support): Asked them to confirm full header and whether they included any extra characters when copying from the vault. They said they copied from an edge worker script in their CDN.

mari (devex): Can you get the raw curl they ran? also ask for a tiny repro if possible.

Customer: 
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: ApiKey sk_live_abc123XYZ;" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

tony (sre): That trailing semicolon is suspicious. Many edge/CDN snippets append a separator when building headers. If the key has to match exactly we will return 401 (invalid_api_key).

sarah (support): @tony can we confirm server-side rejects on exact match? customer wants to know why semicolon breaks it.

tony (sre): Yes. Our auth compares the header token string (trimmed of whitespace) to the stored key. A literal trailing `;` changes the token. We intentionally don't strip punctuation because that could hide client bugs.

mari (devex): Quick repro I ran locally: 
```bash
# works
curl -H "Authorization: ApiKey sk_live_TESTKEY" https://api.test/v1/echo
# fails (401)
curl -H "Authorization: ApiKey sk_live_TESTKEY;" https://api.test/v1/echo
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key is invalid or expired"}

sarah (support): Shared that with the customer and asked them to check their CDN/edge worker code. They replied they were concatenating token + ";" to separate multiple headers when building a list for legacy endpoints.

tony (sre): Recommend they remove the trailing semicolon or URL-decode properly before sending. Also asked them to rotate the key (they already rotated) and confirm new key in edge script has no trailing chars.

mari (devex): Logging suggestion — if you need to guard in the edge worker, do something like: 
```js
const token = SECRET.trim().replace(/;$/, '');
fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `ApiKey ${token}` } })
```

sarah (support): Customer applied the fix and confirmed calls succeeded. They said root cause was a legacy helper that appended `;` to separate multiple creds in one header when migrating from an older internal API.

ci-bot: Deploy note — added a short FAQ item in Support KB: "Why does my API key return 401 when copied from my edge worker?" pointing to trimming/extra-char checklist. :memo:

sarah (support): Closing loop with the customer, marking ticket resolved. :white_check_mark:
